title: Why America Needs a Third Founding
gist: Table of contents and blurb for the Hedgehog Review's Fall 2026 special issue arguing the US needs a third founding comparable to the Revolution and Civil War eras, due November 1. The page has no article body, only contributor titles spanning democracy, wealth concentration and technology.

insights.claim: The Hedgehog Review's Fall 2026 special issue argues the United States needs a refounding as ambitious as the Revolutionary founding or the Civil War-era reconfiguration, to be published November 1.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Signals a rising intellectual push for constitutional and institutional overhaul in US political culture; watch for it entering policy debate.
insights.locator: Why America Needs a Third Founding

insights.claim: The issue is anchored by two pieces by James Davison Hunter, 'The Third Founding Declaration' and 'The Necessity of a Third Founding', which set the framing for the other contributions.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Hunter's framing is the reference point for the argument; his pieces are the ones to read first.
insights.locator: Thematic: Why America Needs a Third Founding

insights.claim: The issue includes essays on economic stewardship (David Ciepley) and on concentrated wealth as a challenge to American democracy (Jeffrey Winters), indicating the refounding case extends to economic structure and not only political institutions.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Wealth concentration is being framed as a constitutional-level problem, which raises long-run political risk for oligarchic-wealth and corporate-power regimes.
insights.locator: Economic Stewardship in the Next American Founding; American Democracy and the Challenge of Concentrated Wealth

themes.theme: Technology and agency in civic life

insights.claim: The issue pairs its refounding argument with pieces on technology and agency (Malloy Owen's 'Agency for Everyone', Antón Barba-Kay's 'The Machine Will Not Go of Itself') and on democratic habits (Sophia Rosenfeld), tying civic renewal to how people live with technology.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Technology governance and civic culture are treated as part of one problem; monitor how this critique shapes tech-skeptical politics.
